title.de: Folge und Gegensatz: so … that, whereas
title.sl: Posledica in nasprotje: so … that, whereas
title.it: Effetto e contrasto: so … that, whereas

goal.sl: Poveš, kaj je iz česa nastalo (so cold that, such a cold night that), postaviš dve dejstvi drugo ob drugo (whereas, nevertheless, on the other hand) in urediš svoj govor (firstly, to sum up, as far as I'm concerned).
goal.de: Du sagst, was woraus wurde (so cold that, such a cold night that), stellst zwei Dinge nebeneinander (whereas, nevertheless, on the other hand) und ordnest deine Rede (firstly, to sum up, as far as I'm concerned).
goal.it: Dici che cosa ne è derivato (so cold that, such a cold night that), metti a confronto due fatti (whereas, nevertheless, on the other hand) e dai ordine al discorso (firstly, to sum up, as far as I'm concerned).
goal.en: You can say what came of something (so cold that, such a cold night that), set two facts side by side (whereas, nevertheless, on the other hand) and keep an argument in order (firstly, to sum up, as far as I'm concerned).

say.sl: **It was so cold that we stayed.** (Bilo je tako mrzlo, da smo ostali.) **so** + pridevnik ali prislov, potem **that** + kar je iz tega nastalo. **Mr Tyson spoke so quietly that nobody heard.** V govoru **that** odpade: **It was so cold we stayed.** To ni **so that** (da bi) iz B1. V Britaniji rečejo tudi *It was that cold we stayed*; v pisanju **so**.
say.de: **It was so cold that we stayed.** (Es war so kalt, dass wir geblieben sind.) **so** + Adjektiv oder Adverb, dann **that** + was daraus wurde. **Mr Tyson spoke so quietly that nobody heard.** Gesprochen fällt **that** weg: **It was so cold we stayed.** Das ist nicht **so that** (damit) aus B1. In Britannien sagt man auch *It was that cold we stayed*; geschrieben **so**.
say.it: **It was so cold that we stayed.** (Faceva così freddo che siamo rimasti.) **so** + aggettivo o avverbio, poi **that** + ciò che ne è derivato. **Mr Tyson spoke so quietly that nobody heard.** A voce **that** cade: **It was so cold we stayed.** Non è **so that** (affinché) del B1. In Gran Bretagna si dice anche *It was that cold we stayed*; per iscritto **so**.
say.en: **It was so cold that we stayed.** **so** + an adjective or an adverb, then **that** + what came of it. **Mr Tyson spoke so quietly that nobody heard.** In talk **that** may go: **It was so cold we stayed.** It isn't B1's **so that** (what for). In Britain people also say *It was that cold we stayed*; writing wants **so**.

say.sl: **It was such a cold night that we stayed.** (To je bila tako mrzla noč, da smo ostali.) **such a**, **such an** + (pridevnik) + samostalnik. Množina in kar se ne šteje sta brez **a**: **We had such bad weather that the bridge closed.** **They are such nice people.** Vrstni red je drugačen kot v slovenščini: najprej **such a**, potem **cold night**.
say.de: **It was such a cold night that we stayed.** (Es war so eine kalte Nacht, dass wir geblieben sind.) **such a**, **such an** + (Adjektiv) + Nomen. Plural und Unzählbares stehen ohne **a**: **We had such bad weather that the bridge closed.** **They are such nice people.** Die Reihenfolge wie bei *so eine kalte Nacht*: erst **such a**, dann **cold night**.
say.it: **It was such a cold night that we stayed.** (Era una notte così fredda che siamo rimasti.) **such a**, **such an** + (aggettivo) + nome. Il plurale e ciò che non si conta stanno senza **a**: **We had such bad weather that the bridge closed.** **They are such nice people.** L'ordine non è quello italiano: prima **such a**, poi **cold night**.
say.en: **It was such a cold night that we stayed.** **such a**, **such an** + (an adjective) + a noun. Plurals and what you can't count have no **a**: **We had such bad weather that the bridge closed.** **They are such nice people.** The order: first **such a**, then **cold night**.

say.sl: **There was so much rain that the beck rose.** (Toliko je deževalo, da je potok narasel.) Pred samostalnikom, ki pove koliko: **so much** za to, česar ne šteješ, **so many** za množino: **There were so many people that the hall was full.** Tudi **so few**, **so little**. Enako pove **such a lot of**: **There was such a lot of rain.**
say.de: **There was so much rain that the beck rose.** (Es regnete so viel, dass der Bach anstieg.) Vor einem Nomen, das sagt, wie viel: **so much** für Unzählbares, **so many** für den Plural: **There were so many people that the hall was full.** Auch **so few**, **so little**. Dasselbe sagt **such a lot of**: **There was such a lot of rain.**
say.it: **There was so much rain that the beck rose.** (Ha piovuto così tanto che il torrente si è alzato.) Davanti a un nome che dice quanto: **so much** per ciò che non si conta, **so many** per il plurale: **There were so many people that the hall was full.** Anche **so few**, **so little**. Lo stesso dice **such a lot of**: **There was such a lot of rain.**
say.en: **There was so much rain that the beck rose.** Before a noun, saying how much: **so much** for what you can't count, **so many** for a plural: **There were so many people that the hall was full.** Also **so few**, **so little**. **such a lot of** says the same: **There was such a lot of rain.**

say.sl: **Jack likes the fell, whereas Sam likes the town.** (Jack ima rad hribe, medtem ko ima Sam rad mesto.) **whereas**, **while** (medtem ko) postavita dve dejstvi drugo ob drugo, z vejico. **while** lahko stoji spredaj: **While Jack likes the fell, Sam likes the town.** **although** iz B1 je za to, kar preseneča: **Although it was cold, we walked.**
say.de: **Jack likes the fell, whereas Sam likes the town.** (Jack mag die Berge, während Sam die Stadt mag.) **whereas**, **while** (während) stellen zwei Dinge nebeneinander, mit Komma. **while** kann vorn stehen: **While Jack likes the fell, Sam likes the town.** **although** aus B1 ist für das, was überrascht: **Although it was cold, we walked.**
say.it: **Jack likes the fell, whereas Sam likes the town.** (A Jack piace il monte, mentre a Sam piace la città.) **whereas**, **while** (mentre) mettono a confronto due fatti, con la virgola. **while** può stare davanti: **While Jack likes the fell, Sam likes the town.** **although** del B1 è per ciò che sorprende: **Although it was cold, we walked.**
say.en: **Jack likes the fell, whereas Sam likes the town.** **whereas**, **while** set two facts side by side, with a comma. **while** can come first: **While Jack likes the fell, Sam likes the town.** B1's **although** is for what surprises: **Although it was cold, we walked.**

say.sl: **The road is narrow. Nevertheless, the bus gets through.** (Cesta je ozka, a avtobus kljub temu pride skozi.) **nevertheless** (kljub temu) je težji **however**: nov stavek, vejica. **on the other hand** (po drugi strani) pove drugo plat: **The car park would bring visitors. On the other hand, it would spoil the tarn.** Lahko tudi prej **on the one hand**.
say.de: **The road is narrow. Nevertheless, the bus gets through.** (Die Straße ist schmal, trotzdem kommt der Bus durch.) **nevertheless** (dennoch) ist ein gewichtigeres **however**: neuer Satz, Komma. **on the other hand** (andererseits) nennt die andere Seite: **The car park would bring visitors. On the other hand, it would spoil the tarn.** Davor auch **on the one hand**.
say.it: **The road is narrow. Nevertheless, the bus gets through.** (La strada è stretta, tuttavia l'autobus passa.) **nevertheless** (tuttavia) è un **however** più solenne: frase nuova, virgola. **on the other hand** (d'altra parte) dice l'altro lato: **The car park would bring visitors. On the other hand, it would spoil the tarn.** Prima anche **on the one hand**.
say.en: **The road is narrow. Nevertheless, the bus gets through.** **nevertheless** is a weightier **however**: a new sentence, a comma. **on the other hand** gives the other side: **The car park would bring visitors. On the other hand, it would spoil the tarn.** Before it, **on the one hand** too.

say.sl: **Firstly, the road is narrow.** (Prvič, cesta je ozka.) Za red v govoru: **firstly**, **secondly**, **finally**, na koncu **to sum up** (če povzamem). Kar misliš: **as far as I'm concerned** (kar se mene tiče), **in my opinion**, **personally**. Tudi **first**, **first of all**, **in conclusion**. **as far as I know** je drugo: kolikor vem.
say.de: **Firstly, the road is narrow.** (Erstens ist die Straße schmal.) Für Ordnung in der Rede: **firstly**, **secondly**, **finally**, am Ende **to sum up** (zusammengefasst). Was du meinst: **as far as I'm concerned** (was mich betrifft), **in my opinion**, **personally**. Auch **first**, **first of all**, **in conclusion**. **as far as I know** ist etwas anderes: soviel ich weiß.
say.it: **Firstly, the road is narrow.** (In primo luogo, la strada è stretta.) Per dare ordine al discorso: **firstly**, **secondly**, **finally**, alla fine **to sum up** (per riassumere). Ciò che pensi: **as far as I'm concerned** (per quanto mi riguarda), **in my opinion**, **personally**. Anche **first**, **first of all**, **in conclusion**. **as far as I know** è un'altra cosa: per quanto ne so.
say.en: **Firstly, the road is narrow.** To keep an argument in order: **firstly**, **secondly**, **finally**, and at the end **to sum up**. What you think: **as far as I'm concerned**, **in my opinion**, **personally**. Also **first**, **first of all**, **in conclusion**. **as far as I know** is another thing: it says what you know.

translation.sl: Bila je tako mrzla noč, da je na sestanek prišlo samo dvajset ljudi. V šoli je bilo tako mrzlo, da smo imeli plašče na sebi. Gospod Tyson hoče parkirišče ob jezercu, gospa Birkett pa ne. »Prvič, cesta je ozka,« je rekla. »Drugič, obiskovalci puščajo smeti. Če povzamem, pokvarilo bi jezerce.« Gospod Tyson je vstal. »Morda imate prav. Kljub temu vas potrebuje denar. Kar se mene tiče, ga moramo zgraditi.«
translation.de: Es war so eine kalte Nacht, dass nur zwanzig Leute zur Versammlung kamen. In der Schule war es so kalt, dass wir die Mäntel anbehielten. Mr Tyson will einen Parkplatz am Bergsee, Mrs Birkett nicht. „Erstens ist die Straße schmal“, sagte sie. „Zweitens lassen Besucher Müll liegen. Zusammengefasst würde es den Bergsee verderben.“ Mr Tyson stand auf. „Vielleicht haben Sie recht. Trotzdem braucht das Dorf das Geld. Was mich betrifft, sollten wir ihn bauen.“
translation.it: Era una notte così fredda che alla riunione sono venute solo venti persone. A scuola faceva così freddo che abbiamo tenuto i cappotti. Il signor Tyson vuole un parcheggio vicino al laghetto, la signora Birkett no. «In primo luogo, la strada è stretta», ha detto. «In secondo luogo, i visitatori lasciano rifiuti. Per riassumere, rovinerebbe il laghetto.» Il signor Tyson si è alzato. «Forse ha ragione. Tuttavia il paese ha bisogno di soldi. Per quanto mi riguarda, dovremmo costruirlo.»
translation.en: It was such a cold night that only twenty people came to the meeting. The school was so cold that we kept our coats on. Mr Tyson wants a car park by the tarn, whereas Mrs Birkett doesn't. “Firstly, the road is narrow,” she said. “Secondly, visitors leave rubbish. To sum up, it would spoil the tarn.” Mr Tyson stood up. “You may be right. Nevertheless, the village needs the money. As far as I'm concerned, we should build it.”
